questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

1. Project Elephant was launched in 1992 to protect elephants in India.

2. Project Tiger was launched in 1973 to conserve tigers in India

3. Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve is located in West Bengal, India.

4. Keoladeo National Park is located in Madhya Pradesh.

Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1, 2, 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Project Elephant** was launched by the **Government of India** in **February 1992** as a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme** to provide financial and technical support to states for the protection of elephants, their habitats, and corridors. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Project Tiger** was launched on **April 1, 1973**, at **Jim Corbett National Park** to ensure a viable population of the **Bengal Tiger** in India and to preserve areas of biological importance as a natural heritage. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The **Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve**, located in the **Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta** in **West Bengal**, is the largest mangrove forest in the world and was designated as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1987**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Keoladeo National Park**, formerly known as the **Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary**, is located in **Bharatpur**, **Rajasthan**, not Madhya Pradesh. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Project Tiger** is administered by the **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)**, a statutory body under the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change**.
 
• The **Sundarbans** is a unique ecosystem known for the **Royal Bengal Tiger** and was designated as a **Ramsar Site** of international importance in **January 2019**.
 
• **Keoladeo National Park** is a **man-made wetland** and a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**, famous for hosting thousands of birds, including the critically endangered **Siberian Crane** during winters.
 
• **Project Elephant** also focuses on addressing issues of **Human-Elephant Conflict** and the welfare of domesticated elephants through the **MIKE (Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants)** program.

questions.question: Which policy, approved in August 2024, aims to accelerate innovation-driven research and entrepreneurship in high-performance biomanufacturing in India?

questions.question: What was Raja Ram Mohan Roy's greatest social achievement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abolition of Sati in 1829**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**, often regarded as the **Father of the Indian Renaissance**, was a pioneer of social and religious reform in 19th-century India.
 
• His most significant social achievement was the relentless campaign against **Sati**, a cruel practice where widows were immolated on their husbands' funeral pyres. He argued that this custom had no basis in authentic **Hindu scriptures** like the **Upanishads**.
 
• He founded the **Brahmo Sabha** in **1828** (later **Brahmo Samaj**), which provided a structured platform to advocate for **monotheism** and the **abolition of social evils**.
 
• Roy's persistent advocacy and petitions influenced **Lord William Bentinck**, the then Governor-General of India, to pass the **Sati Regulation Act XVII** on **December 4, 1829**.
 
• This landmark legislation initially declared **Sati** illegal and punishable as **culpable homicide** in the **Bengal Presidency**, and it was subsequently extended to **Madras** and **Bombay** in 1830.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Promoting English education**:

 
 
• Roy was a staunch supporter of **modern Western education** to modernize Indian society.
 
• He assisted **David Hare** in establishing the **Hindu College** in 1817 and founded the **Vedanta College** in 1825, which integrated **Indian learning** with **Western physical and social sciences**.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress (INC)**:
 
 
• The **INC** was founded in **1885** by **Allan Octavian Hume**, over five decades after Roy's death in **1833**.
 
 
 
• **Abolition of child marriage**:
 
 
• While Roy opposed the practice, the formal **Child Marriage Restraint Act** (also known as the **Sarda Act**) was not enacted until **1929**.
 
• Other reformers like **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar** (who focused on **widow remarriage**) and **B.M. Malabari** were instrumental in later legislative successes against child marriage.
 
 
 
• **Journalism**:
 
 
• He utilized the press to influence public opinion, publishing the Bengali journal **Sambad Kaumudi** and the Persian newspaper **Mirat-ul-Akbar**.

questions.question: What was the theme for International Mother Language Day 2025?

options.text: Using technology for multilingual learning: Challenges and opportunities
Silver Jubilee Celebration of International Mother Language Day
Multilingual Education: A necessity to transform education
Multilingual education – a pillar of learning and intergenerational learning

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Silver Jubilee Celebration of International Mother Language Day**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **International Mother Language Day** is celebrated every year on **21 February** to promote linguistic and cultural diversity and the importance of **multilingualism**.
 
• The day was first proclaimed by the **UNESCO General Conference** in **November 1999** and has been observed worldwide since **February 2000**.
 
• The year **2025** marks the **Silver Jubilee** (25th anniversary) of this global initiative, celebrating a quarter-century of efforts to preserve and protect **mother tongues**.
 
• The theme specifically acknowledges the historical milestone reached since the first celebration in **2000**, highlighting the long-term commitment of **UNESCO** and its member states to **linguistic diversity**.
 
• The observance has its roots in the **Language Movement** of **Bangladesh** (formerly East Pakistan), where students and activists sacrificed their lives in **1952** to establish **Bangla** as an official state language.
 
• The 25-year milestone in **2025** serves as a platform to evaluate the progress of the **International Decade of Indigenous Languages (2022−2032)** and the integration of **mother languages** in digital and educational spaces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other themes associated with the recent history of **International Mother Language Day** include:

 
 
• **Using technology for multilingual learning: Challenges and opportunities**: This was the official theme for **2022**, focusing on the potential of technology to support **multilingual education**.
 
• **Multilingual Education: A necessity to transform education**: This served as the theme for **2023**, emphasizing the shift towards inclusive **mother-tongue-based** learning environments.
 
• **Multilingual education - a pillar of learning and intergenerational learning**: This was the official theme for **2024**, stressing the role of native languages in passing knowledge between generations.

questions.question: In which year was the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) launched?
questions.solution:

• The **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY)** was launched on **1st July 2015**, which falls under the financial year **2015-16**, with the motto of **'Har Khet Ko Pani'**.
 
• The primary objective of the scheme is to achieve **convergence of investments** in irrigation at the field level, expand the cultivable area under **assured irrigation**, and improve **on-farm water use efficiency** to reduce wastage of water.
 
• The scheme was formulated by amalgamating ongoing schemes such as the **Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme (AIBP)**, the **Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP)**, and the **On Farm Water Management (OFWM)** component of the **National Mission on Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA)**.
 
• It focuses on creating protective irrigation by harnessing rainwater through **'Jal Sanchay'** and **'Jal Sinchan'** at the micro level to enhance agricultural productivity and generate rural employment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Main Components of PMKSY**:

 
 
• **Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme (AIBP)**: Monitored by the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**, it aims at the faster completion of ongoing **Major and Medium Irrigation** projects.
 
• **Har Khet Ko Pani (HKKP)**: Focuses on the creation of new water sources through **Minor Irrigation** (both surface and ground water) and the restoration of traditional water bodies.
 
• **Per Drop More Crop (PDMC)**: Managed by the **Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare**, this component promotes **Micro-irrigation** technologies like **Drip** and **Sprinkler** systems to maximize water productivity.
 
• **Watershed Development**: Implemented by the **Department of Land Resources**, it emphasizes effective management of runoff water and improved **soil and moisture conservation** activities.

questions.question: When Barium Chloride (BaCl₂) solution is mixed with Sodium Sulfate (Na₂SO₄) solution, a white product Barium Sulfate (BaSO₄) is formed. This product is known as a ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Precipitate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a solution of **Barium Chloride (BaCl₂)** is mixed with **Sodium Sulfate (Na₂SO₄)**, a **double displacement reaction** occurs where the ions of the two salts exchange partners.
 
• The chemical equation for this process is: **BaCl₂ (aq) + Na₂SO₄ (aq) → BaSO₄ (s) + 2NaCl (aq)**.
 
• The resulting **Barium Sulfate (BaSO₄)** is a white, **insoluble solid** that does not dissolve in water and settles at the bottom of the container.
 
• In chemistry, any solid that forms and separates from a liquid solution during a chemical reaction is scientifically defined as a **Precipitate**.
 
• The formation of **Barium Sulfate** is often used in laboratories as a qualitative test to confirm the presence of **Sulfate ions** in a given sample.
 
• Since **Barium Sulfate** is the solid product emerging from the aqueous mixture, it is correctly identified as a **Precipitate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Emulsion**:

 
 
• A mixture of two or more **immiscible liquids** where one is dispersed in the other, such as **oil in water**.
 
• They are stabilized by agents called **emulsifiers** and are common in food products like **milk** and **butter**.
 
 
 
• **Isomer**:
 
 
• Compounds that share the exact **same molecular formula** but have different **structural arrangements** or spatial configurations.
 
• Because of these differences in bonding, **isomers** typically exhibit distinct **physical and chemical properties**.
 
 
 
• **Isotope**:
 
 
• Variants of a particular chemical element which possess the same number of **protons** (same atomic number) but a different number of **neutrons**.
 
• This leads to differences in **atomic mass**, such as the difference between **Carbon-12** and **Carbon-14**.

questions.question: In Windows 11 File Explorer, which feature is used to quickly locate a file by typing its name?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Search box** is a dedicated input field located in the **top-right corner** of the **Windows 11 File Explorer** interface, used for performing **real-time queries**.
 
• It allows users to quickly find **files**, **folders**, and **sub-directories** by typing their **file names**, **file extensions** (such as .docx or .pdf), or specific **keywords** found within the file content.
 
• The feature utilizes the **Windows Search Indexing** service, which pre-scans files to provide near-instant results; users can also use **keyboard shortcuts** like **Ctrl + F** or **F3** to activate it immediately.

questions.question: Which Padma Shri awardee was given the title of Nritya Samragini by Rabindranath Tagore?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sitara Devi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sitara Devi** (1920–2014) was a legendary exponent of **Kathak**, a classical dance form of North India, and is widely credited with bringing the dance style to the global stage and mainstream **Indian Cinema**.
 
• The title **Nritya Samragini**, which translates to the **Empress of Dance**, was bestowed upon her by the Nobel Laureate **Rabindranath Tagore** after he witnessed her performance in **Mumbai**.
 
• The historical encounter took place when **Sitara Devi** was only **sixteen years old**; she performed a three-hour long **Kathak** recital at the **Tata Palace** in the presence of **Tagore** and other luminaries like **Sarojini Naidu**.
 
• Deeply impressed by her rhythmic precision and expressive power, **Tagore** invited her to **Shantiniketan** and presented her with a ceremonial shawl and a gold coin as a mark of respect along with the iconic title.
 
• She belonged to the **Banaras Gharana** of Kathak and was trained by her father, **Sukhadev Maharaj**, who was a renowned scholar and dancer himself.
 
• Over her illustrious career, she was honored with the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** in **1969** and the **Padma Shri** in **1973** for her immense contribution to the performing arts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kanak Rele**:

 
 
• She was a world-renowned **Mohiniyattam** dancer and the founder-director of the **Nalanda Dance Research Centre** in **Mumbai**.
 
• She was instrumental in the scientific systematization of **Mohiniyattam** and received the **Padma Bhushan** in **2013**.
 
 
 
• **Sobha Naidu**:
 
 
• A prominent disciple of **Vempati Chinna Satyam**, she was an eminent **Kuchipudi** dancer known for her mastery over the **Satyabhama** and **Padmavati** roles.
 
• She served as the principal of the **Kuchipudi Art Academy** in **Hyderabad** and was awarded the **Padma Shri** in **2001**.
 
 
 
• **T. Balasaraswati**:
 
 
• A seventh-generation representative of the traditional **Devadasi** heritage, she is regarded as the **Queen of Bharatanatyam**.
 
• She was the first dancer to be awarded the **Padma Vibhushan** in **1977** and played a key role in gaining international recognition for **South Indian** classical dance.

questions.question: Which tree species is most commonly associated with India’s tropical deciduous forests?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Teak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tropical Deciduous Forests** are the most widespread forest type in India, often referred to as **Monsoon Forests**. They cover nearly **65 percent** of India's total forest area.
 
• **Teak (Tectona grandis)** is the most dominant and commercially valuable tree species found in these forests. It is particularly characteristic of the **Moist Deciduous** subtype, which thrives in regions receiving rainfall between **100 cm and 200 cm**.
 
• These forests are found on the eastern slopes of the **Western Ghats**, the **Chhota Nagpur Plateau**, and throughout **Central India**. Significant populations are located in **Madhya Pradesh**, **Maharashtra**, **Karnataka**, and **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• The defining feature of species like Teak in these regions is the **seasonal shedding of leaves** for approximately six to eight weeks during the dry summer months to prevent water loss through transpiration.
 
• Teak is prized for its high-quality **hardwood**, which contains natural oils making it resistant to termites and weather, essential for **shipbuilding** and premium **furniture**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Comparison with other forest species:
 
 
• **Fir**: A coniferous tree belonging to **Montane Forests**. It is found at high altitudes in the **Himalayan region**, typically above 2,500 meters.
 
• **Oak**: A broad-leaved species common in **Wet Temperate Forests**. In India, they are found in the **Himalayas** at altitudes between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
 
• **Pine**: Specifically the **Chir Pine**, it is the most common tree in **Subtropical Pine Forests**, found in the lower altitudes of the Himalayan belt.
 
• **Sal**: Along with Teak, **Sal** is a major deciduous species, but it is more prevalent in the **northeastern parts** of the peninsula and the **Himalayan foothills**.

questions.question: If a ball is thrown vertically upward, which of the following describes its velocity at the highest point?

options.text: Equal to acceleration due to gravity

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zero**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an object is thrown vertically upward, it moves against the force of Earth's **Gravity**, which provides a constant downward **Acceleration** (g ≈ 9.8 m/s²).
 
• As the object rises, its **Initial Velocity** decreases at a steady rate due to this downward acceleration, a process known as **Deceleration** or **Retardation**.
 
• The **Highest Point** represents the peak of the trajectory where the object reaches its maximum vertical displacement from the point of release.
 
• To transition from an upward motion to a downward motion, the object's velocity must pass through a state of **Instantaneous Rest**; therefore, the magnitude of its velocity at that exact moment is **0 m/s**.
 
• Using the first equation of motion, **v = u − gt**, at the maximum height (t = u/g), the final velocity (**v**) equates to exactly **Zero**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acceleration vs Velocity**:

 
 
• A common misconception is that acceleration is also zero at the peak. However, the **Acceleration due to Gravity** remains constant and non-zero (9.8 m/s² downward) throughout the motion. If it were zero, the ball would stop and float rather than falling back down.
 
 
 
• **Directional Sign Convention**:
 
 
• In physics, velocity is a **Vector Quantity**. If upward motion is defined as **Positive**, the velocity is positive during ascent and **Negative** during descent.
 
• The value **Zero** marks the critical point where the direction of the vector flips.
 
 
 
• **Energy Distribution**:
 
 
• At the highest point, the ball's **Kinetic Energy** (1/2 mv²) is zero because the velocity is zero.
 
• Conversely, its **Gravitational Potential Energy** (mgh) is at its maximum, representing the total mechanical energy of the system in the absence of air resistance.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Article established the office of Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities?

• The article mandates that there shall be a **Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities** to be appointed by the **President of India**. The officer is designated as the **Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities**.
 
• The primary duty of this officer is to investigate all matters relating to the safeguards provided for **linguistic minorities** under the Constitution. This includes monitoring the implementation of constitutional provisions and administrative schemes related to language rights.
 
• The Special Officer submits reports to the **President** at such intervals as the President may direct. These reports are subsequently laid before each **House of Parliament** and sent to the governments of the **States** concerned.
 
• The office of the **Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities** was established in **1957**, with its headquarters located at **Prayagraj (Allahabad)**, and it operates under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Minority Affairs**.

questions.question: A Local Area Network (LAN) enables resource sharing by connecting devices to the network medium through a specialized adapter called the __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Network Interface Card**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Network Interface Card (NIC)** is a hardware component, typically a circuit board or chip, installed on a computer that allows it to connect to a **Local Area Network (LAN)** and other networks.
 
• The NIC operates at both the **Physical Layer** (Layer 1) and the **Data Link Layer** (Layer 2) of the **Open Systems Interconnection (OSI)** model, providing the necessary hardware circuitry for data transmission.
 
• Each card has a unique, permanent identification number called the **Media Access Control (MAC) address**, which is used to direct traffic to the specific device on the network.
 
• The NIC acts as a translator, converting the computer's internal **Parallel Data** into **Serial Data** signals that can travel over network cables (like **Ethernet**) or through the air via radio waves (for **Wireless NICs**).
 
• It manages the flow of data packets between the computer and the transmission medium, ensuring that data is transmitted at a speed compatible with the network standard, such as **10/100/1000 Mbps**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Graphics Processing Unit (GPU)**:

 
 
• A specialized processor designed to accelerate **Graphics Rendering** and image processing.
 
• Commonly used in **Gaming**, video editing, and complex mathematical computations like **Machine Learning**.
 
 
 
• **Read-Only Memory (ROM)**:
 
 
• A **Non-Volatile** memory type that permanently stores data required to start the computer.
 
• It contains the **BIOS (Basic Input/Output System)** or **UEFI** firmware that performs the initial hardware checks.
 
 
 
• **Central Processing Unit (CPU)**:
 
 
• Referred to as the **Brain of the Computer**, it interprets and executes most of the commands from hardware and software.
 
• Consists of the **Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)** for calculations and the **Control Unit (CU)** for managing instruction cycles.

questions.question: Tribunals under Article 323A (Administrative tribunals) of the Constitution of India can be established by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 323A** of the **Constitution of India** specifically provides for the establishment of **Administrative Tribunals** for the adjudication of disputes relating to the recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to public services.
 
• According to Clause (1) of **Article 323A**, the power to create such tribunals is vested exclusively in the **Parliament** by law; it does not grant this specific power to **State Legislatures** or the **Judiciary**.
 
• This article was inserted into the Constitution through the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, which introduced a new **Part XIV-A** titled **Tribunals**.
 
• In pursuance of **Article 323A**, the **Parliament** enacted the **Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985**, which authorized the **Central Government** to establish the **Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT)** and **State Administrative Tribunals (SATs)**.
 
• Even when a **State Administrative Tribunal** is established for a particular state, it is done by an act of **Parliament** (upon the request of the respective state government), confirming that the legislative competence remains with the **Union Parliament** only.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 323B**:

 
 
• Unlike **Article 323A**, which is restricted to **public service matters**, **Article 323B** allows for the creation of tribunals for various other matters such as **taxation**, **foreign exchange**, **land reforms**, **ceiling on urban property**, and **elections**.
 
• Under **Article 323B**, both the **Parliament** and the **State Legislatures** have the authority to establish tribunals within their respective legislative fields.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review**:
 
 
• In the landmark **L. Chandra Kumar vs. Union of India (1997)** case, the **Supreme Court** ruled that the decisions of these tribunals are subject to the **judicial review** of **High Courts**.
 
• This means that while the **Parliament** establishes them, the **High Courts** and the **Supreme Court** maintain supervisory jurisdiction over them as part of the **basic structure** of the Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following is a landlocked inland river port in India?

• The port is a critical component of **National Waterway 2** (NW-2), which connects **Dhubri** and **Sadiya**. It is meticulously managed by the **Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI)**.
 
• Functioning as a **multimodal transport hub**, it facilitates the transit of **bulk cargo** such as coal, cement, and food grains via the **Indo-Bangladesh Protocol (IBP)** route, linking the landlocked North East to the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Unlike coastal ports that handle oceanic vessels, **Pandu port** is designed for **inland water transport (IWT)** vessels and barges that navigate river systems.

questions.question: India followed which strategy to reduce dependence on foreign goods after independence?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Import substitution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• After independence in **1947**, India adopted an **inward-looking trade strategy** known as **Import Substitution Industrialization (ISI)** to achieve **self-reliance** and reduce its vulnerability to the global economy.
 
• The primary objective of this policy was to protect **domestic industries** (often called **infant industries**) from foreign competition by replacing imports with **indigenous production**.
 
• This strategy was heavily emphasized during the **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961)**, which was based on the **Mahalanobis Model** focusing on heavy industries and capital goods.
 
• The government implemented this through two main instruments: **Tariffs** (imposing high taxes on imported goods to make them less attractive) and **Quotas** (specifying the maximum quantity of goods that could be imported).
 
• By restricting foreign goods, the government aimed to save **foreign exchange reserves** and promote the growth of local manufacturers in sectors like electronics, automobiles, and machinery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Export-led growth**:

 
 
• This is an **outward-looking** strategy where a country seeks to grow its **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** by focusing on producing goods for the international market.
 
• Unlike India's early approach, this was successfully utilized by **East Asian Tigers** like South Korea and Taiwan.
 
 
 
• **Free trade**:
 
 
• A policy where the government does not discriminate against imports or interfere with exports by applying **tariffs** or **subsidies**.
 
• India moved toward this model only after the **1991 Economic Reforms**, which introduced **Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG)**.
 
 
 
• **Dollarisation**:
 
 
• A process where a country officially adopts the **United States Dollar** as its **legal tender** alongside or instead of its domestic currency.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are true or false regarding Sleep and Hibernate modes in Windows 11?

(i) Hibernate saves the session to the hard disk before shutting down, allowing full recovery upon restart.

(ii) Sleep consumes more power than Hibernate because it keeps the RAM powered.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(i) True, (ii) True**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hibernate mode** in **Windows 11** is a power-saving state designed primarily for laptops; it takes all currently open **applications** and **system metadata** and writes them to the **hard disk** or **SSD** into a hidden file called **hiberfil.sys**. This process allows the computer to be powered off completely while ensuring that the **user session** is fully restored exactly as it was when the machine is turned back on. ***Hence, statement (i) is correct.***
 
• **Sleep mode**, also known as **Standby** or **S3 State**, maintains the current session in the **Random Access Memory (RAM)**. Because **RAM** is **volatile memory**, it requires a continuous, albeit small, amount of **electrical power** to prevent data loss, whereas **Hibernate** (an **S4 State**) requires effectively zero power because the session is stored on non-volatile **physical storage**. ***Hence, statement (ii) is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparison of Power States:**

 
 
• **Sleep Mode:** It offers the fastest **resume time** (often 1-2 seconds) because the **CPU** does not need to reload data from the disk. It is ideal for short breaks during work but risks data loss if the battery dies.
 
• **Hibernate Mode:** While it has a slower **startup time** compared to sleep, it is safer for long periods of inactivity as it does not drain the **battery** and is immune to power outages.
 
• **Hybrid Sleep:** A feature mostly used on **desktop computers** that combines both modes; it puts the session in **RAM** for speed but also writes it to the **hard drive** as a backup in case of a **power failure**.
 
• **Fast Startup:** A **Windows** feature that uses **hibernation technology** to save the **operating system kernel** to the disk during shutdown, enabling faster **boot times** upon the next start.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Emergency provisions is true?

options.text: Convert the federal system into a unitary one

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Convert the federal system into a unitary one**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Emergency Provisions** are contained in **Part XVIII** of the **Constitution of India**, from **Article 352 to Article 360**, designed to protect the **sovereignty, unity, and integrity** of the nation.
 
• During the proclamation of an emergency, the **Central Government** acquires the power to direct any state regarding the manner in which its executive power is to be exercised, effectively overriding the **federal distribution of powers**.
 
• The unique feature of the **Indian Constitution** is its ability to transform from a **federal structure** to a **unitary structure** during emergencies without requiring a formal **Constitutional Amendment** under **Article 368**.
 
• This shift ensures that the **Union Government** can respond decisively to extraordinary situations like war, internal disturbances, or financial instability by centralizing **legislative and executive authority**.
 
• **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** noted that while most federal systems are "placed in a tight mould of federalism," the Indian system is unique as it can be both **unitary as well as federal** according to the requirements of time and circumstances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Types of Emergencies in India:
 
 
• **National Emergency (Article 352)**: Triggered by **war, external aggression, or armed rebellion**. It suspends the **Fundamental Rights** under **Article 19** automatically and others via Presidential order.
 
• **President's Rule (Article 356)**: Imposed when the **constitutional machinery** in a state fails, allowing the President to assume the functions of the **State Government**.
 
• **Financial Emergency (Article 360)**: Proclaimed if the **financial stability** or credit of India is threatened; it allows the Centre to reduce the **salaries and allowances** of all classes of persons serving the Union or States.
 
 
 
• Incorrect Concepts:
 
 
• **Monarchy**: India is a **Democratic Republic**, meaning the **Head of State** (President) is elected, and emergency provisions do not alter this fundamental status.
 
• **Federalism continuation**: While the federal structure exists in normal times, it is temporarily suspended or "unitatized" during an emergency to ensure **national security**.

questions.question:
Which statement is True or False about System Software?

(i) The Operating System runs in privileged mode, giving it unrestricted access to hardware.

(ii) Core System Software like device drivers is essential for the computer to start and function.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(i) True, (ii) True**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operating Systems** function using a dual-mode operation to protect the system. The **Kernel**, which is the core part of the **Operating System**, executes in **Privileged Mode** (also known as **Kernel Mode** or **Supervisor Mode**). In this state, the **CPU** has unrestricted access to all **Hardware**, **Memory**, and **System Instructions**, allowing it to manage resources and perform low-level tasks that **User Applications** cannot. ***Hence, statement (i) is correct.***
 
• **System Software** serves as the interface between the hardware and the user. **Device Drivers** are specialized programs that allow the **Operating System** to communicate with specific hardware components like **Hard Drives**, **Graphics Cards**, and **Network Adapters**. Without these core components, the **Operating System** would be unable to initialize hardware during the **Boot Process** or manage data flow, making them essential for the computer to start and function. ***Hence, statement (ii) is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **System Software Categories**:

 
 
• **Operating System (OS)**: Software like **Windows**, **Linux**, or **macOS** that manages **CPU Scheduling** and **Memory Allocation**.
 
• **BIOS/UEFI**: The primary **Firmware** that performs the **Power-On Self-Test (POST)** and initializes hardware during startup.
 
• **Utility Software**: Tools like **Disk Defragmenters** and **Antivirus** that maintain system efficiency.
 
 
 
• **CPU Execution Modes**:
 
 
• **User Mode**: A restricted mode where **Application Software** runs to prevent it from accessing critical memory or hardware directly.
 
• **Privileged Mode**: Reserved for the **OS Kernel**; it uses **Protection Rings** (usually **Ring 0**) to ensure system stability and security.

questions.question: Which of the following is a method specifically used to control particulate air pollution?

options.text: Use of fabric filters to trap dust and fly ash
Increasing chimney height without any treatment
Absorption of gases using liquid scrubbers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Use of fabric filters to trap dust and fly ash**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fabric filters**, commonly referred to as **baghouses**, are specialized industrial air pollution control devices designed to remove **particulate matter (PM)** from flue gas or exhaust streams.
 
• They function by passing contaminated air through a series of long, cylindrical bags made of **woven or felted fabric**, which physically trap solid pollutants such as **dust**, **soot**, and **fly ash**.
 
• The filtration process involves several physical mechanisms including **inertial impaction**, **interception**, and **diffusion**; as the operation continues, a **dust cake** forms on the fabric, which significantly increases the removal efficiency of **fine particulates**.
 
• These systems are highly effective for **particulate control**, often achieving collection efficiencies of over **99 percent** for particles as small as **0.5 to 1 micrometer** in diameter.
 
• They are essential in **high-pollution industries** such as **thermal power plants**, **cement factories**, and **metal smelting** units to prevent the release of harmful **fly ash** into the atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Absorption of gases (Liquid Scrubbers)**:

 
 
• This method primarily targets **gaseous pollutants** like **Sulfur Dioxide (SO2)** and **Nitrogen Oxides (NOx)** by dissolving them in a **liquid solvent** (often water or an alkaline solution).
 
• While **wet scrubbers** can capture some particulates, the specific process of **absorption** is a mass-transfer operation meant for chemical gas removal rather than solid particle filtration.
 
 
 
• **Catalytic Combustion**:
 
 
• This technique is used to treat **Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs)** and **Carbon Monoxide (CO)** by oxidizing them at lower temperatures using a **catalyst** (such as **Platinum** or **Palladium**).
 
• It does not effectively remove **non-combustible particulates** like mineral dust or ash.
 
 
 
• **Increasing Chimney Height**:
 
 
• A **dispersion strategy** that utilizes **stack height** to release pollutants higher into the atmosphere, allowing for **dilution** by wind before they reach ground level.
 
• This is not a **control method** as it does not reduce the **total mass** of pollutants emitted into the environment.
 
 
 
• **Electrostatic Precipitators (ESP)**:
 
 
• Another major device for **particulate control** that uses **electric charges** to collect particles on large **collector plates**, widely used for managing **fine fly ash** in **coal-fired power stations**.

questions.question: Which of the following elements is malleable and a good conductor of heat and electricity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Barium (Ba)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Barium (Ba)** is a chemical element classified as an **alkaline earth metal**, located in **Group 2** and **Period 6** of the periodic table with the **atomic number 56**.
 
• As a metallic element, Barium possesses the physical property of **malleability**, meaning it can be hammered, pressed, or rolled into thin sheets without breaking or cracking.
 
• It is an effective **conductor of heat and electricity** because its metallic lattice contains **delocalized valence electrons** that are free to move and transport energy throughout the material.
 
• While Barium is a **soft, silvery-white metal**, it is highly reactive, particularly with water and oxygen, which is why it is often stored in mineral oil to prevent oxidation.
 
• In comparison to the other options, Barium is the only true **metal**; the others are non-metals or noble gases which lack the **metallic bonding** necessary for conductivity and malleability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sulfur (S)**:

 
 
• It is a **non-metal** with the atomic number **16**.
 
• In its common solid form (S₈), it is extremely **brittle** and will crumble into powder when struck, making it the opposite of malleable.
 
• It acts as an **insulator** because it lacks free electrons to facilitate electrical or thermal flow.
 
 
 
• **Iodine (I)**:
 
 
• A **halogen** and non-metal with the atomic number **53**.
 
• Although it appears as a dark, **lustrous solid** at room temperature, it is physically brittle and a **poor conductor**.
 
 
 
• **Neon (Ne)**:
 
 
• A **noble gas** with the atomic number **10** belonging to **Group 18**.
 
• It is a colorless, odorless **monatomic gas** under standard conditions, meaning properties like malleability are not applicable.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Uses of Barium**:
 
 
• **Barium sulfate (BaSO₄)** is used as a **radiocontrast agent** for X-ray imaging of the gastrointestinal tract.
 
• It is also utilized as a **getter** in vacuum tubes to remove residual trace gases due to its high chemical reactivity.

questions.question: At the 2025 World Aquatics Championships, which male swimmer set a new world record in the 200 m individual medley (IM) during semifinals?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution places the most emphasis on reducing income and status disparities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 38(2)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 38(2)** of the **Indian Constitution** specifically mandates that the **State** shall strive to minimize **inequalities in income**.
 
• It further directs the government to endeavor to eliminate inequalities in **status**, **facilities**, and **opportunities** among individuals and groups of people.
 
• This clause is unique because it targets disparities not only between **individuals** but also among **groups of people** residing in different areas or engaged in different **vocations**.
 
• The provision is a vital part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**, which provide a roadmap for establishing a **welfare state** and ensuring **economic justice**.
 
• By focusing on **income and status**, this article serves as the constitutional basis for progressive taxation, **subsidies**, and various **affirmative action** programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978**:

 
 
• **Article 38(2)** was not originally in the Constitution; it was inserted by the **44th Amendment** during the **Morarji Desai**-led **Janata Party** government to reinforce **socialist goals**.
 
 
 
• **Article 38(1)**:
 
 
• This clause focuses on the broader concept of **social order**, directing the State to promote the **welfare of the people** by securing **social, economic, and political justice**.
 
 
 
• **Article 39**:
 
 
• This article lists specific principles like the **right to an adequate livelihood**, **equal pay for equal work**, and the prevention of the **concentration of wealth** in a few hands.
 
 
 
• **Article 36**:
 
 
• It defines the term **'State'** for the purpose of **Part IV** (DPSP), carrying the same meaning as defined under **Article 12** in **Part III**.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains the emergence of “megaregions” with extremely high population densities (e.g., Bos Wash, Tokyo-Osaka, Pearl River Delta)?

options.text: They exist because of high natural population growth in these regions
They develop due to integrated economic corridors and high connectivity
Governments intentionally relocate populations to form megaregions
Megaregions form primarily because of uniform physical geography

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They develop due to integrated economic corridors and high connectivity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Megaregions** are vast networks of metropolitan areas that share environmental systems, infrastructure, and integrated economic activities, often spanning hundreds of miles.
 
• The development of these regions is driven by **agglomeration economies**, where the clustering of businesses, labor, and services leads to increased productivity and innovation.
 
• **Integrated economic corridors**, such as high-speed rail, multi-lane expressways, and advanced telecommunications, allow for the seamless movement of **goods, services, and human capital** across city boundaries.
 
• For instance, the **Tokaido Corridor** in **Japan** is a quintessential megaregion where the **Shinkansen** (bullet train) has physically and economically linked **Tokyo**, **Nagoya**, and **Osaka**, enabling them to function as a single urban system.
 
• The **Pearl River Delta** in **China** demonstrates how **high connectivity** through massive bridges and port infrastructure has turned a cluster of cities into a global manufacturing and technology powerhouse.
 
• Unlike **natural population growth**, which occurs locally, megaregions emerge through **economic magnetism** that attracts migrants and investment from across the globe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Northeast Megalopolis (BosWash)**:

 
 
• First identified by geographer **Jean Gottmann** in **1961**, stretching from **Boston** to **Washington, D.C.**
 
• It contains less than **2%** of **United States** land area but produces approximately **20%** of the national **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**.
 
• Connectivity is sustained by the **I-95 corridor** and the **Northeast Corridor** rail line, facilitating intense financial and political exchange.
 
 
 
• **The Pearl River Delta (Greater Bay Area)**:
 
 
• Consists of nine mainland cities plus **Hong Kong** and **Macau**, forming the most densely populated urban area in the world.
 
• It is a **polycentric urban region** where specific cities specialize in manufacturing (Dongguan), finance (Hong Kong), and technology (Shenzhen).
 
 
 
• **Conceptual Differences**:
 
 
• **Natural Growth vs. Integration**: While natural birth rates contribute to population, the defining feature of a megaregion is the **functional integration** of separate cities.
 
• **Physical Geography**: While many megaregions are coastal, geography alone does not create them; rather, the **man-made infrastructure** (ports and airports) leveraging that geography is what drives the density.

questions.question: In the context of periodicity, elements in the same group tend to display similar chemical properties. Which primary factor is responsible for this similarity among group members?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Similar valence electronic configuration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **Modern Periodic Table**, elements are arranged in vertical columns called **groups** and horizontal rows called **periods**. The chemical behavior of an element is primarily determined by its **electronic configuration**, specifically in the outermost shell.
 
• The **valence shell** is the outermost electron shell of an atom, and the electrons residing there are called **valence electrons**. Elements in the same group possess the **same number of valence electrons**, leading to a **similar valence electronic configuration**.
 
• Chemical reactions involve the redistribution of electrons (losing, gaining, or sharing) to achieve a stable state, often following the **octet rule**. Since elements in a group have the same number of electrons available for bonding, they tend to form similar types of **chemical bonds** and compounds.
 
• For instance, all elements in **Group 1** (Alkali Metals) have a general outer configuration of **ns¹**, meaning they all have one valence electron. This commonality makes them all highly reactive, as they easily lose that single electron to form **+1 cations**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atomic Number**:

 
 
• Each element has a **unique atomic number** representing the number of protons in its nucleus. While the atomic number increases sequentially across a period and jumps by specific intervals down a group, it is never **identical** for any two elements.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Radius**:
 
 
• The **atomic radius** is the distance from the center of the nucleus to the outermost shell. Within a group, the atomic radius **increases** from top to bottom due to the addition of new **principal energy levels** (shells). Therefore, it is not a **constant** factor.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Mass**:
 
 
• This is the weighted average mass of an atom's isotopes. In any group, the **atomic mass** increases significantly as we move down, meaning it is not a factor that remains **similar** or dictates group-wise chemical similarity.

questions.question: Which highly revered Śvetāmbara Jain text describes the lives of the 24 Tīrthaṅkaras, the lineage of pontiffs, and the monastic rules observed during the Paryuṣaṇa festival?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalpa-sutra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kalpa-sutra** is a foundational religious text in **Jainism**, specifically belonging to the **Svetambara** tradition, and is traditionally attributed to the monk **Bhadrabahu**, who lived in the **4th century BCE**.
 
• The text is structurally divided into three sections: the first part, **Jinacharita**, provides detailed hagiographies of the **24 Tirthankaras**, focusing heavily on the lives of **Mahavira**, **Parshvanatha**, **Neminatha**, and **Rishabhanatha**.
 
• The second section, known as the **Theravali**, chronicles the **succession of disciples** and the **lineage of pontiffs** (spiritual leaders) who maintained the Jain teachings after the **Nirvana** of **Lord Mahavira**.
 
• The final section, **Samachari**, prescribes the **monastic rules** and codes of conduct specifically for the rainy season (**Varshavas**), which are ritually recited by monks during the **Paryushana** festival.
 
• It serves as a primary source for understanding early **Jain history**, the evolution of monastic discipline, and the transition of the faith from oral traditions to written scriptures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Paryushana Festival**:

 
 
• This is the most important annual holy event for Jains, where the **Kalpa-sutra** is publicly read and explained to the laity over several days.
 
• It emphasizes **repentance** (Pratikramana), **fasting**, and the study of sacred scriptures to achieve spiritual purification.
 
 
 
• **Artistic and Historical Significance**:
 
 
• The **Kalpa-sutra** manuscripts are famous for their **miniature paintings**, representing some of the earliest examples of the **Western Indian school of art**.
 
• The author, **Bhadrabahu**, was the spiritual teacher of the **Mauryan Emperor Chandragupta** and is credited with preserving Jain knowledge during a great famine in **Magadha**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary association of the Ektara, a folk musical instrument?

options.text: Martial arts performances in Chhau dance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Folk and devotional string music**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ektara** is a traditional **one-stringed instrument** widely recognized as one of the simplest string instruments used in the Indian subcontinent. The name is derived from the Hindi words **Ek** meaning 'one' and **Tara** meaning 'string'.
 
• It is primarily utilized as a **drone instrument** to provide a basic rhythmic and melodic foundation for singers, particularly in **folk** and **devotional** contexts.
 
• The instrument is the soul of the **Baul music** tradition of **West Bengal** and **Bangladesh**, where wandering mystic minstrels use it to accompany their spiritual songs.
 
• It also holds a significant place in **Sufi music** and **Bhakti movement** traditions across **Maharashtra**, **Punjab**, and **Uttar Pradesh**, often used by saints and bards during **Kirtans** and **Bhajans**.
 
• Structurally, it consists of a **resonator** (usually a dried **gourd**, **wood**, or **coconut shell**) covered with skin, and a split **bamboo** neck that the player squeezes to vary the tension of the string and change the pitch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Folk Traditions and Variations**:

 
 
• In **Maharashtra**, the Ektara is frequently used by **Warkari** pilgrims and **Haridasa** singers to praise **Lord Vitthal**.
 
• In the **Punjab** region, a similar version is used in **folk ballads** and traditional storytelling.
 
• It is often played alongside other folk instruments like the **Duggi** (a small drum) or **Khamak** to create a rich rhythmic layer for **mystical poetry**.
 
 
 
• **Other Regional Contexts**:
 
 
• **Chhau Dance**: Unlike the Ektara, this martial dance primarily uses loud percussion and wind instruments like the **Dhol**, **Nagada**, and **Shehnai** to match its energetic movements.
 
• **Temple Rituals in Odisha**: These typically involve instruments like the **Mardala** (pakhawaj variant) and **Shankha** (conch shell), which are distinct from the nomadic nature of the Ektara.
 
• **Court Dances**: Classical forms like **Bharatanatyam** rely on sophisticated string instruments like the **Saraswati Veena** rather than simple folk drones.
